svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.14.2.1 Foundation Wall Drainage
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.14 DRAINAGE
Foundation Wall Drainage

g.text: Tile or pipe laid around the exterior of
Or a layer of gravel or crushed rock
Mineral fibre insulation against the wall
Crushed rock backfill extends to the footing

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Unless it can be shown to be unnecessary, the
bottom of every exterior foundation wall is
drained
By drainage tile or pipe laid around the exterior
of the foundation in conformance with Subsection
9.14.3., or by a layer of gravel or crushed rock
in conformance with Subsection 9.14.4.
Where mineral fibre insulation or crushed rock
backfill is against the exterior of a
foundation wall, it extends to the footing
level to help ground water drain to the
foundation's drainage system
Any pyritic material in the crushed rock is
limited to a concentration that will not
damage the building to a degree that would
adversely affect its stability or the
performance of assemblies
Drawn: basement walls cut through, soil cut back. Note A-9.14.2.1.(2)(a): such a layer does not replace dampproofing or waterproofing.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.14.2.1. (page 9-115)
